👁 SEE

I can…
  • I can open PSD documents and image assets in Photoshop.
  • I can use the Quick Selection Tool and Lasso Tool to select subjects accurately.
  • I can separate a subject onto its own layer using Layer via Copy.
  • I can reorder layers and adjust opacity and blend modes like Soft Light to create composition depth.
Key ideas
  • Layer organization and sandwich composition order
  • Subject selection using Quick Selection and Lasso tools
  • Refining selections by adding or subtracting using modifier keys
  • Using Layer via Copy for non-destructive placement
  • Applying layer opacity adjustments and Soft Light blend modes
Vocabulary
Compositing — Combining multiple image assets and layers into a single cohesive scene.
Quick Selection Tool — A tool used to quickly paint and automatically select an image subject based on edge detection.
Layer via Copy — A command that places selected pixels onto a brand new separate layer.
Lasso Tool — A freehand selection tool used to manually draw and refine selection boundaries.
Blending Mode — A setting in the layers panel that determines how a layer's pixels blend with the underlying layers.
Opacity — The degree to which a layer is transparent or opaque.
Soft Light — A layer blending mode used to create subtle lighting effects and a distant appearance.
Sandwich Composition — The vertical arrangement of layers in the layers panel that dictates what appears in front of or behind other elements.

🧠 CHECK

Which tool is used to paint over and select the scuba diver from the background?
Answer: The Quick Selection Tool is selected from the toolbar to paint over and select the scuba diver subject.
How do you subtract unwanted water areas from your selection around the air hose?
Answer: Holding down the Alt key allows you to subtract unwanted water areas from the selection around the air hose.
What command should you choose when right-clicking a selection to place it on its own separate layer?
Answer: You right-click the selection and choose Layer via Copy to place the selected subject on its own layer.
Why should you avoid moving the copied layer after placing the subject on its own layer?
Answer: Do not make a copy of the layer and move it, because it ruins the illusion. The whole point of making a copy is to tuck things behind that layer without moving it.
Which blending mode is used to give the appearance that a graphic is further in the distance with visible bubbles?
Answer: The blending mode is changed to Soft Light to give the appearance that the graphic is further in the distance.
What key is held down to subtract unwanted areas from a selection?
Answer: Holding down the Alt key subtracts unwanted water areas from the selection.
What action is performed by dragging a layer down to the plus sign icon?
Answer: Dragging a layer to the plus sign icon duplicates it.
What blend mode is applied to give the graphic a distant appearance with visible bubbles?
Answer: Setting the blending mode to Soft Light achieves this distant, blended effect.

🛠 When it breaks

⚠ The selected subject includes unwanted background water or cuts off part of the air hose.
Why: Automatic edge detection included background pixels or missed fine details.
Fix: Hold down the Alt key to subtract unwanted areas or switch to the Lasso tool to manually refine the selection.
Prevent: Zoom in closely on the subject edges before painting your selection.
⚠ The scuba diver appears in front of the shark instead of behind it.
Why: The scuba diver layer is placed above the shark layer in the layers panel.
Fix: Drag the shark layer above the scuba diver layer in the layers panel.
Prevent: Always verify layer hierarchy after compositing multiple elements into a scene.
